name: Zoom

verdict.headline: A Zoom General app works in your own account right away, but other accounts can use it only through a Zoom-approved beta share (10 account-level / 100 user-level additions, 3–4 business days) or a full two-phase Marketplace review with a security review and no stated SLA.
verdict.nextAction: Create the General app, install it in your own account with Local Test, and start the Technical Design section now, because both beta sharing and publishing need it.

appType: General app (OAuth) on the Zoom App Marketplace

paths.name: Beta sharing (up to 10 accounts / 100 users)
paths.whenThisApplies: You need a limited number of users outside your own Zoom account to test the app before it is published.

timeline.label: Create app, set scopes, local test
Technical Design section and supporting evidence
timeline.note: Beta approval comes after requirements are met. The 2 days–2 weeks estimate covers the full prerequisite list (TDD, privacy, terms, docs, support, deauth endpoint).

timeline.label: Zoom approves the Request to Share
timeline.note: 72 hours after requirements are met; "no longer than 3–4 business days". Approval is case by case.

timeline.label: Customer admin installs or pre-approves
timeline.note: Depends on the customer's org. A Zoom account may require a Marketplace admin to pre-approve the app.

paths.name: Published Marketplace app
paths.whenThisApplies: Any Zoom account should be able to install the app, including as an unlisted public listing.

timeline.label: Create app, set scopes, local test
TDD, privacy policy, terms, docs, support URL, deauth endpoint
Production credentials, listing, test plan, test account
Two-phase Marketplace review including security review
timeline.note: Zoom's docs state no fixed timeline. Secondary (Zoom staff on the developer forum, Dec 2025): a 72-hour SLA excluding weekends and US holidays, and the security queue "can take up to 2 weeks".

timeline.label: Customer admin installs or pre-approves
timeline.note: Depends on the customer's org. A Zoom account may require a Marketplace admin to pre-approve the app.

beforeApproval.item: Development and private apps work only inside your own Zoom account
beforeApproval.detail: Add the app from Local Test ("Add App Now") and share the authorization URL with members of your account. "You can only share private apps with members within your Zoom account."

beforeApproval.item: External beta sharing needs Zoom's approval
beforeApproval.detail: Use Production > Beta Test > "Request to Share". Zoom approves each request case by case.

beforeApproval.item: Beta cap: 10 additions for an account-level app, 100 for a user-level app
beforeApproval.detail: Ask marketplace.security@zoom.us for a higher limit; those requests are reviewed "within 24hrs".

beforeApproval.item: Beta URL lasts 4 weeks, plus two 4-week extensions (about 90 days)
beforeApproval.detail: Users who already added the app keep access after the URL expires. The URLs stop working once the app is published.
An unlisted public listing still needs the full review.
Private and development apps don't send deauthorization notifications, so you can't test that flow before production.

prerequisites.item: A Zoom account with developer permissions, and a management type chosen at creation
prerequisites.detail: Admin-managed: account admins install the app and it can reach data for users across the account. User-managed: any individual user can install it and it sees only that user's data.

prerequisites.item: A redirect URL and an OAuth allow list
Technical Design section completed, with supporting evidence
prerequisites.detail: Zoom says it prefers to see a Secure Software Development Lifecycle (SSDLC).

prerequisites.item: Terms of Use, Privacy Policy, self-serve documentation and a Support URL

prerequisites.detail: It must verify Zoom's signature with the secret token and delete the user's data.

steps.title: Create a General app
steps.detail: Go to Marketplace > Develop > Build an app > General app. Set the name and management type (admin-managed or user-managed).

steps.title: Configure OAuth and wire up the flow
steps.detail: Configure the OAuth redirect URL and allow list, then wire up the authorize and token flow.

steps.title: Choose features and scopes, with a justification for each scope
steps.detail: Adding a scope "is actually submitting a request to the Zoom Security Review team".
steps.agentHelp: Draft a justification for each scope and flag scopes the code doesn't use.

steps.title: Install the app in your own account with Local Test
steps.detail: Use Local Test ("Add App Now") to install the app in your own account.

steps.title: Build token handling, the deauth webhook and event webhooks
steps.detail: Build token caching and refresh handling, the deauthorization webhook, and webhooks to use instead of polling.

steps.title: Fill in the Technical Design section
steps.detail: Complete the Technical Design section with supporting evidence. Optionally use Request to Share for a beta.
steps.agentHelp: Draft the Technical Design content and the supporting evidence from the codebase.

steps.title: Zoom approves the beta share
steps.detail: 72 hours after requirements are met; no longer than 3–4 business days.

steps.title: Switch to production and submit
steps.detail: Switch to production credentials. Complete the listing, test plan, test account, docs, privacy policy and support URL, then submit.
steps.agentHelp: Draft the privacy policy, terms, self-serve docs (including how to remove or deauthorize the app), the test plan and a pre-submission checklist.

steps.title: Zoom runs the review
steps.detail: Completeness and branding; functionality, usability and compliance; security (TDD review, scope minimisation and OWASP Top 10 testing).

steps.title: Work through the remediation report and resubmit
steps.detail: Address each item in the remediation report, then resubmit.
steps.agentHelp: Map each remediation item to a code or document fix and draft the responses.

steps.title: Customer admin installs or pre-approves the app
steps.detail: "A Zoom account may require an app be pre-approved by a Marketplace admin."

submissionChecklist.item: Accurate metadata, name, description, images and video
A test plan and a test account or credentials
A documentation URL with actionable content
submissionChecklist.detail: Including how to remove or deauthorize the app.

submissionChecklist.item: Privacy Policy, Terms of Use and Support URL

submissionChecklist.detail: Not confirmed as a requirement. Videos appear only as a listing asset.

gotchas.title: Access tokens last 1 hour, refresh tokens 90 days, and refresh tokens rotate
gotchas.detail: Always store and use the latest refresh token.

gotchas.title: Calling /oauth/token before every request gets apps rejected
gotchas.detail: Cache the access token and refresh it only when needed.

gotchas.title: Development and production credentials are different
Changing management type changes available features and scopes
gotchas.detail: Recheck both features and scopes after changing it.

gotchas.title: Granular scopes (2024) replaced classic scopes for new apps
gotchas.detail: Classic apps can migrate with the Migrate button.

gotchas.title: Production may still return classic scopes
gotchas.detail: Forum users report problems with production still returning classic scopes.

gotchas.title: The required TDD format has changed before
gotchas.detail: Developers have been rejected as "incomplete" for using an old format.

gotchas.title: Meeting SDK: OBF or ZAK token required from 2 March 2026
gotchas.detail: Meeting SDK apps that join meetings hosted by other accounts need an OBF or ZAK token, or RTMS. This applies only if your General app embeds the SDK.

blockers.symptom: External testers can't authorize the app
blockers.whatToDo: Request a beta share, or publish the app.
Email Zoom to ask for a higher limit; requests are reviewed within 24 hours.
Remove unused scopes and write a justification for each one that remains.
Check the reviewer notes in the dashboard, then post in the devforum Marketplace > Submission category.

unknowns: Zoom's docs give no official SLA for public review. The 72-hour and security-queue figures come only from Zoom staff on the developer forum.
Whether a demo video or a separate security questionnaire is required, beyond the TDD.
Any 2025 changes to the General app build flow beyond granular scopes.
Whether production still returns classic scopes for some apps (forum user reports only).
Whether Developer Support paid plans are a working escalation path for Marketplace review.
